Does a Home Warranty Cover Slab Leaks in Florida?

By SRQ Leak Pros Editorial · Published November 5, 2026 · Updated November 5, 2026 · 7 min read

Short answer: Sometimes. Some home warranty plans cover slab leak repair, often with a dollar cap and only for the pipe itself. Others exclude slab leaks or sell coverage as an add-on. Damage to floors, walls and belongings is usually not covered by the warranty. Read your contract, and check your homeowners policy for the damage side.

Does a home warranty cover slab leaks? The honest answer is that it depends on the contract. Coverage varies widely between plans. If you have a leak under your floor, SRQ Leak Pros can connect you with a local provider for slab leak repair in Sarasota while you sort out who pays.

This is general information, not legal or insurance advice. Every contract and policy differs.

What is a home warranty in Florida?

A home warranty is a service contract, not an insurance policy. Florida law defines it in § 634.301 of the Florida Statutes. A home warranty is a contract in which a company agrees to repair or replace parts of a home that fail from normal wear. The statute calls the seller a home warranty association. It's an organization other than an authorized insurer that issues home warranties.

The same statute defines a structural component as the roof, plumbing system, electrical system, foundation, walls, ceilings or floors of a home. So the law expects some warranties to cover plumbing, but each contract sets its own terms.

Does a home warranty cover slab leaks at all?

Some do. ConsumerAffairs reports that some plans include slab leaks in standard coverage, some sell it as an add-on and some exclude it. When covered, the plan usually pays for the pipe repair, not the damage around it.

ItemOften covered by a warranty?
Finding the leakSometimes, within plan limits
Repairing the leaking pipeSometimes, up to a dollar cap
Breaking and patching the slabOften limited or excluded
Rerouting the lineVaries by plan
Flooring, drywall and cabinetsUsually not
Mold and dryingUsually not
BelongingsNo

ConsumerAffairs gives an example: a plan may fix the pipe that caused the leak but not replace damaged flooring.

Common slab leak exclusions

ConsumerAffairs lists common reasons plans deny slab leak claims:

  • Preexisting conditions
  • Lack of regular maintenance
  • Root intrusion
  • Freezing
  • Improper installation
  • Accidental damage

Many contracts also cap what they'll spend on access through concrete. Some limit the repair method, such as allowing a spot repair but not a reroute.

Home warranty vs. homeowners insurance for slab leaks

The two can work together, but they pay for different things.

QuestionHome warrantyHomeowners insurance
What is it?Service contractInsurance policy
Typical focusRepairing worn systemsSudden, accidental damage
Pipe repairSometimesOften not the pipe itself
Water damageUsually notOften, if covered
Who regulates?Florida Chapter 634 rulesFlorida insurance law

For the insurance side, Florida Statutes § 627.70132 sets claim deadlines. For most new claims, notice is due within one year of the date of loss. Our guide on whether insurance covers slab leaks explains that side in detail.

How to file a home warranty claim for a slab leak

  1. Stop the water. Close the main shut-off if water is rising or the meter is spinning.
  2. Call the warranty company first. Many plans require you to report the leak right away.
  3. Wait for authorization. ConsumerAffairs notes that plans often require approval before repairs start.
  4. Check the waiting period. New plans may have a waiting period before coverage starts, often 15 to 30 days per ConsumerAffairs.
  5. Document everything. Photos, meter readings, dates and every call.
  6. Get the diagnosis in writing. Ask for the leak location and cause.
  7. Ask about the cap. Learn the limit before work starts.
  8. Call your insurer too. If water damaged floors or walls, report that separately.

What does a slab leak cost if the warranty won't pay?

Angi's national data puts slab leak detection at about $280 on average and slab leak repair at about $2,300 on average, including detection. Reroutes and repipes cost more. See the slab leak repair cost guide for the details that move a quote.

Can you use your own plumber with a home warranty?

Usually not without approval. Most plans send their own contractor. If you call your own provider first, the plan may deny the claim. Read the contract. If water is causing damage and you can't reach the company, stop the water, document why you acted and keep every receipt.

Slab homes in Sarasota and warranty coverage

Most Sarasota homes sit on a concrete slab foundation, with water lines under or inside the slab. Home warranties are often bought or gifted at closing. Read the plumbing section before you need it. Look for the words slab leak, access, concrete and caps. Seasonal owners should check whether an unoccupied home or a delayed report changes coverage.

How to protect yourself before a slab leak

  • Read the plumbing and slab sections of your contract now.
  • Ask whether slab leak coverage is an add-on.
  • Write down the access cap and repair limits.
  • Keep maintenance records and inspection reports.
  • Check your meter monthly for small leaks.

What slab leak repairs do warranties usually pay for?

Plans differ most on the repair method. A slab leak can be fixed in three main ways, and a warranty may pay for one but not the others.

Repair methodWhat it involvesHow warranties often treat it
Spot repair through the slabBreak a small opening, fix the pipe, patchOften covered up to an access cap
RerouteRun a new line through walls or the attic, abandon the old oneSometimes covered, sometimes limited
RepipeReplace a full section or the whole systemOften excluded or capped
Pipe liningCoat the inside of the old pipeVaries widely

Ask the warranty company which method they approve before work starts. If you prefer a reroute but the plan pays only for a spot repair, ask whether they'll put the spot repair amount toward the reroute.

How caps, waiting periods and service fees affect a claim

Three terms decide most of what you'll pay:

  • Dollar caps. Many plans limit what they spend on one item or one claim. A slab leak can reach that limit fast.
  • Waiting periods. New contracts often have a waiting period before coverage starts. ConsumerAffairs reports most last 15 to 30 days.
  • Service fees. Most plans charge a fee each time a contractor visits. Check the amount in your contract.

Read the plumbing section and the limits page side by side. A plan that lists slab leaks as covered may still cap the access work.

What to do if your warranty denies a slab leak claim

  1. Ask for the reason in writing. Note which contract clause they cite.
  2. Compare it to your contract. Look for the slab, access and exclusion sections.
  3. Get a second diagnosis. A separate leak detection report can confirm the cause.
  4. Keep repairing the damage. Don't let water keep running while you dispute it.
  5. Escalate. Ask for a supervisor or the claims review team.
  6. Check your insurance. The water damage side may still be a homeowners claim.

Should you add slab leak coverage to a home warranty?

It depends on your home and your budget. Ask these questions before you buy:

  • Is the home on a slab with supply lines under the floor?
  • How old are the pipes, and what are they made of?
  • What is the access cap, in dollars?
  • Does the add-on cover reroutes, or only spot repairs?
  • Are leak detection costs included?
  • What exclusions apply to older pipe?

If your supply lines already run through the attic, a slab leak add-on may matter less. A drain line under the slab can still leak, so check whether drains are covered too.

Local note: slab-on-grade homes are common in North Port and Venice. Seasonal homes in Longboat Key can hide a leak for weeks, which may affect a claim.

  • You hear running water with every tap off
  • Floors feel warm or damp in one spot
  • The warranty denies the claim or caps it low
  • You need a second opinion on the repair method

Frequently asked questions

Is a home warranty the same as insurance in Florida?

No. Florida law treats a home warranty as a service contract issued by a home warranty association, not an authorized insurer.

Will a home warranty pay to break up my floor?

Some plans pay for limited access through concrete up to a cap. Others exclude it. Read the access terms in your contract.

Does a home warranty cover water damage from a slab leak?

Usually not. Warranties tend to cover the pipe repair. Water damage is more often a homeowners insurance question.

What if my warranty denies a slab leak claim?

Ask for the reason in writing and compare it to your contract. You can also file a complaint with Florida's insurance regulators, who oversee home warranty associations.
